 The high-quality action on the LPGA Tour continues this week, as Taiheiyo Club’s Minori Course hosts the Toto Japan Classic. A $2 million purse is up for grabs, with the field taking on the 6,608-yard, par-72 layout in Omitama, Japan. Here are the latest LPGA Tour betting odds and our Toto Japan Classic picks for 2026.
 Thursday, Nov 5 to Sunday, Nov 8 · Taiheiyo Club Minori Course, Omitama, Japan · Golf Channel

 Toto Japan Classic Preview: Players to Watch
 The Toto Japan Classic has been a mainstay on the LPGA Tour since 1973, with Annika Sörenstam the dominant force in the early 2000s, winning it five times between 2001 and 2005.
 Nasa Hataoka
 Hataoka is an obvious starting point as the defending champion. She has played at a high level all season, including a T6 at the U.S. Women’s Open and a T15 at the Women’s PGA Championship.
 Miyuu Yamashita
 Yamashita arrives as the favorite and in red-hot form after winning last week’s Maybank Championship. The 25-year-old Japanese star has finished in the top 10 in each of her last five starts, a run that also includes a win at the CPKC Women’s Open.
 Jeeno Thitikul
 Thitikul should be well rested for her return this week, having last played when finishing T8 at the LPGA Shanghai. The 22-year-old has finished in the top 10 in each of her last 10 starts, winning twice in that run.

 Toto Japan Classic Picks and Golf Betting Tips
 Rio Takeda already knows how to win this event, having lifted the trophy in 2024, and that makes her +3300 price look generous. She’s one of the fastest-rising stars on the LPGA Tour and has been consistent all season, making the cut in 16 of her 22 starts.
 She had a frustrating weekend at the recent BMW Ladies Championship, but if she gets back to the form that saw her finish fourth at the LPGA Shanghai and T13 at the Lotte Championship, she has every chance of a second Toto Japan Classic title. With Yamashita and Thitikul taking up so much of the betting at the top, Takeda is the value play.
 Best bet: Rio Takeda to win (+3300)
